data.title: Artery forceps
data.summary: Forceps & clamps · Ring-handled locking clamp with blunt serrated tapering jaws used to catch bleeders and grasp tissue.
data.body:
![Artery forceps](instruments/artery-forceps.jpg)

_Also called: Haemostatic forceps, Hemostat, Mosquito forceps, Kelly clamp, Crile / Rochester-Pean forceps_

Ring-handled locking clamp with blunt serrated tapering jaws used to catch bleeders and grasp tissue.

## Parts
- Ring handles
- Ratchet lock
- Box joint
- Blunt tapering jaws with transverse serrations

## Types / variants
- Straight or curved
- Mosquito (Halsted/Hartmann) - smallest, 3-5 inch
- Kelly - 5-7 inch, serrations on distal part of jaw only
- Crile / Rochester-Pean - largest, serrations along entire jaw

## Uses / indications
- Catching bleeding vessels
- Holding the free end of a suture
- Blunt dissection of lipoma and cysts
- Crushing the pedicle of pedunculated lesions (acrochordon, DPN)
- Removing nail plate in partial nail avulsion
- Three-point traction during circumcision
- Plucking hairs for trichogram

## How to hold
Thumb and ring finger in the rings, index finger along the shanks for control; ratchet engaged/released by pressing the rings together and apart.

## Sterilisation & care
Autoclave, hot air oven, 2% glutaraldehyde or boiling

## Viva points & tips
- Size order: Mosquito < Kelly < Crile/Pean
- Medium and small sizes are most used in dermatosurgery (PPT1)
